summary: Live chat websocket stalls mid-generation when passing through edge transcoding proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports websocket-based streaming chat sessions intermittently stalling mid-generation when traffic flows through the company's edge transcoding proxy. Stalls occur several seconds into generation and are followed by client-side timeout or silent stream closure. This began after an edge service change rolled 2026-03-04 (transcode-proxy v3.7.1).

Impact:
- Multiple active chat sessions for Papertrail AI (Dedicated) experienced mid-token stalls leading to user-visible timeouts and ticketed customer interruptions. Estimated ~12% of long-stream requests (>512 token responses) in us-west-2 show the symptom since the deploy.

Environment:
- Customer: Papertrail AI (Dedicated)
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Edge component: transcode-proxy cluster (edge-proxy pool a)
- Serving runtime: rw-13b-v1 pinned for customer

Steps to reproduce:
1) Establish websocket connection to /v1/chat/stream with streaming enabled and a prompt that triggers >600 token response.
2) Observe token stream for first ~3s–10s.
3) In affected runs, stream yields a continuous chunk sequence then experiences a quiet gap (typically 4–9s) mid-token and never resumes; client eventually times out or connection closes.

Observed behavior:
- Quiet interval between chunks measured at 4.7s–8.9s mid-generation (examples in logs).
- No 5xx logged by serving runtime; api-gateway shows a 504 for associated websocket upgrade request in some cases.
- Packet-level traces show TLS record coalescing and long gaps from the proxy side.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous token delivery for duration of generation with minimal inter-chunk latency (<1s typical).

Logs / snippets:
- Example timeline (ISO timestamps):
  2026-03-06T14:12:03.112Z: first chunk (token 0..47)
  2026-03-06T14:12:03.879Z: subsequent chunks streaming
  2026-03-06T14:12:09.023Z: quiet gap begins
  2026-03-06T14:12:17.095Z: client reports connection closed / timeout
- Edge proxy logs show repeated BufferFlush events and a change in flush heuristics after v3.7.1 deploy.
- pcap/tcpdump from customer path attached in ticket (link to S3 provided in Slack).

Investigation notes so far:
- Timeline correlates onset with transcode-proxy v3.7.1 deployed 2026-03-04 (release notes mention "adaptive TLS framing and response coalescing").
- Local repro only when traffic is routed through transcode-proxy; bypassing it (direct to edge-gateway) does not reproduce.
- SRE observed higher variance in TLS record sizes and fewer flushes from proxy to backend; likely interaction between response coalescing and websocket framing/keepalive behavior leading to long quiet windows while a token is being produced.
- No evidence that serving-runtime itself is crashing or returning 5xx; token generation continues on worker side based on kv-cache traces.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Rolled transcode-proxy pool back to v3.6.8 for a subset of nodes handling Papertrail AI traffic; observed reduction in stall rate from ~12% -> ~1.5% for that shard.
- Short-term customer workaround: use non-streaming completion endpoint (polling) or request server-sent chunk flush by setting header X-Flush-Stream: true (internal header honored by older proxy builds).

Next steps / proposed fixes:
- SRE to coordinate rollback of transcode-proxy v3.7.1 (in progress) or patch to disable the aggressive coalescing heuristics for websocket upgraded connections.
- Engineering to add automated regression test for websocket continuous-flush behavior in edge-proxy CI harness.
- Request PR to add explicit streaming-flush header passthrough (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412 included initial draft).

Owner: Jonas Meyer (SRE)
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 UTC - Aisha Patel: Customer opened with logs attached. Reports many long-chat sessions drop around 6–8s into generation. Marking P1 due to live user impact.

2026-03-05 09:45 UTC - Support (Aisha): Raised to SRE oncall and posted links to Grafana (streaming token latency dashboard) and the customer's pcap in #support. Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/papertrail-stalls-03-05

2026-03-05 10:20 UTC - SRE (Jonas): Noted correlation with edge-proxy rollout 2026-03-04; requested full transcode-proxy logs and a tcpdump from customer's egress path. Also requested allocation of a rollback window for v3.7.1.
2026-03-05 13:55 UTC - Customer (Papertrail AI, Maya Chen): Uploaded tcpdump and confirmed behavior reduces when routing directly to gateway (bypass transcode-proxy).

2026-03-06 02:06 UTC - SRE (Jonas): Performed partial rollback for customer shard to v3.6.8; early metrics look promising (stall rate dropped to ~1.5% for that shard). Will monitor for 24h before broader roll-back/patch.

2026-03-07 16:30 UTC - Eng (Luis Fernandez): Created PR to add websocket-aware flush control to edge-proxy (see PR 412). Planning tests to simulate steady token stream and enforce empty-chunk flush interval < 500ms.

2026-03-09 11:02 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer acknowledged mitigation and asked for timeline for full rollout of fix; noted that papertrail will accept a coordinated maintenance window for full rollback if necessary.
resolution: Partial mitigation: shard rollback to transcode-proxy v3.6.8 decreased failure rate. Engineering patch drafted to add explicit websocket flush control. Rollback/patch schedule pending SRE change window.
